title: Assistant Accountant
description:
Assistant Accountant

Grimsby Full-time Permanent £30k-£33k per annum

Are you an ambitious finance professional looking for a broad, hands-on accounting role where you can develop your skills and make a real impact?

I'm currently recruiting for an Assistant Accountant to join a well-established and growing organisation. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys working across a wide range of finance activities, from management accounts and reporting through to treasury, forecasting, audit support and business analysis.

Reporting directly to the Head of Finance, you'll play a key role in delivering accurate and insightful financial information to senior stakeholders. This is a varied position that offers exposure to multiple areas of finance, providing excellent development opportunities for someone looking to progress their career.

Key responsibilities include:
- Supporting monthly, half-year and annual financial reporting processes.
- Assisting with budgeting, forecasting, VAT returns and management reporting.
- Preparing journals, maintaining accounting records and providing variance analysis with meaningful commentary.
- Completing balance sheet reconciliations and supporting strong financial controls.
- Managing bank reconciliations, cash flow forecasting and supplier payment runs.
- Processing purchase invoices, raising purchase orders and issuing sales invoices.
- Supporting credit control activities and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Maintaining fixed asset registers and year-end reporting schedules.
- Assisting with annual audit requirements, statutory accounts preparation and financial modelling projects.

This opportunity would suit an organised and analytical individual who enjoys problem-solving and working collaboratively across a business.

We're keen to speak with candidates who have:
- Previous experience within a finance or accounting role.
- Strong attention to detail and a proactive approach to their work.
- Good Excel and Microsoft Office skills.
- The ability to communicate financial information clearly to a range of stakeholders.
- Experience working with accounting systems.
- A flexible mindset and willingness to support ongoing finance projects.

An accountancy qualification, or active study towards one, would be advantageous but is not essential.

What's in it for you?
- A varied and rewarding finance role with exposure to senior stakeholders.
- Opportunities to develop your technical and commercial finance skills.
- A supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Competitive salary and benefits package.
- Employer pension contribution.
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Long-term career development opportunities within a growing organisation.

If you're looking for your next step in finance and would like to join a business where you can genuinely add value and broaden your experience, I'd love to hear from you.

Apply today with your CV to be considered.

title: Private Client Secretary
description:
Private Client Legal Secretary

Lincoln Full Time Office Based 26,000 - 29,000 Maternity Cover from November 2026 with potential opportunities beyond the initial contract

The best Legal Secretaries are often the people who quietly hold everything together.

They're the person who keeps a busy department organised, makes clients feel looked after and ensures that even the busiest days run smoothly. If that sounds like you, this could be a fantastic opportunity.

We're working with a long-established Lincoln law firm with an excellent reputation and, just as importantly, a reputation for looking after its people. In a profession where movement between firms can be common, many members of the team have built long and successful careers here. People stay because they're valued, trusted and genuinely enjoy being part of the firm.

This opportunity has arisen as a valued member of the team prepares to go on maternity leave. To allow for a thorough handover, the successful candidate will join in November 2026 ahead of maternity leave commencing in January. Whilst initially offered on a fixed-term basis, there is a realistic possibility that opportunities could exist beyond the maternity cover period.

Working closely with an experienced, busy and approachable Head of Department, you'll support a broad range of Private Client matters including Wills, Probate, Powers of Attorney and Estate Administration. You'll manage diaries and appointments, prepare correspondence and legal documentation, liaise with clients and professional contacts and help ensure matters continue progressing smoothly and efficiently.

More than anything, this role would suit somebody who loves being organised, enjoys creating structure and takes pride in being the person others rely on. Previous legal secretarial experience would be preferred, but we're equally interested in speaking with strong secretaries who have developed their skills within professional services environments, including strong audio typing skills and are looking for a role where they can make a genuine difference.

Perhaps you're looking for a firm where your contribution will be recognised. Maybe you'd like to work more closely with an experienced lawyer who values good support. Or perhaps you're simply looking for a business where people stay because they enjoy being there.

Whatever your reason for considering a move, opportunities like this don't come around very often. A respected local firm, a supportive manager, a proper handover, meaningful work and the chance to become part of a team where people build careers rather than simply pass through.

If you're highly organised, professional and take real pride in helping others succeed, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today for a confidential conversation and discover why so many people choose to stay with this firm for the long term.

title: Operational Administrator

We are seeking a proactive, organised and commercially minded Operational Administrator to join a busy FMCG operation at our Boston site.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys being at the heart of business operations. You'll play a key role in supporting the smooth running of the operation, taking responsibility for stock administration, product costings, customer order profiles, reporting and customer queries.

Working closely with colleagues across the business, you'll help ensure operational processes run efficiently, information is accurate and customer expectations are consistently met.

Operational Administrator Key Responsibilities
- Stock Management: Maintain accurate stock records, monitor stock levels and investigate discrepancies, ensuring stock information is always up to date.
- Costings: Prepare, review and update product costings, ensuring accuracy and supporting effective cost management.
- Order Profiles: Create and maintain customer order profiles, ensuring orders are accurately recorded and processed efficiently.
- Reporting: Produce daily summaries and operational reports, providing accurate information to support business performance.
- Customer Queries: Handle customer enquiries professionally, resolving issues promptly and maintaining strong customer relationships.
- Operational Support: Work closely with internal teams to support daily operations, maintain efficient processes and ensure deadlines are consistently achieved.

Operational Administrator About You
- Previous experience in an operational administration, stock control or order processing role, ideally within FMCG.
- Strong numerical skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Confident using IT systems, with good Microsoft Office skills.
- Highly organised, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- A proactive problem-solver with a positive, can-do attitude.
- Excellent communication skills and a customer-focused approach.
- Experience using the Prophet system would be advantageous but is not essential.

Operational Administrator What's on Offer?
- Salary: £29,870 per annum.
- Working days: Wednesday to Saturday.
- Hours: 7:00am 5:30pm.

title: Goods In Administrator
description:
Goods In Administrator

Location: Scunthorpe
Hours: 8:30am until 4:30pm Monday to Friday
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience

About the Company

Our client is a well-established, family-owned business operating within the UK steel distribution and processing industry, with over 160 years of heritage.

Operating across 29 sites throughout the UK and Ireland, the business holds more than 120,000 tonnes of steel stock and has built an outstanding reputation for delivering quality products and exceptional customer service.

Despite its significant size and presence within the industry, the business remains committed to its people, customers and local communities. Continued investment in employees, modern processing machinery, technology and materials-handling equipment ensures the business remains at the forefront of the industry.

This is a forward-thinking organisation that values hard work, ambition, teamwork and fresh ideas, offering an excellent opportunity to join a business where people genuinely matter.

About the Role

We are currently recruiting for an experienced Goods In Administrator to join a friendly and supportive team within a busy warehouse and manufacturing environment.

This is a varied administrative position, providing essential support across the Goods In and wider operations functions. The successful candidate will play an important role in ensuring incoming materials are accurately received, recorded and processed, whilst also providing general administrative and customer service support.

The role would suit someone who is highly organised, has excellent attention to detail and enjoys working in a busy environment where no two days are the same.

Key Responsibilities
- Answer incoming telephone calls, directing enquiries to the appropriate departments or individuals.
- Welcome visitors and assist with their movements whilst onsite.
- Process stock amendments as required, including printing and checking stock adjustment reports.
- Raise and process invoices, purchase orders and goods receipting notes.
- Manage incoming emails, responding appropriately or forwarding to the relevant departments.
- Ensure the accurate and efficient receipt of incoming materials in line with Goods Inwards schedules and procedures.
- Check test certifications and material documentation, ensuring all material standards and requirements are maintained.
- Carry out regular stock checks, identifying and correcting any discrepancies.
- Monitor incoming stock rotations, ensuring materials are presented with the correct colour coding and cast numbers.
- Ensure cut confirmation records are accurate and communicated to the relevant teams.
- Liaise with operational colleagues regarding daily work plans and priorities.
- Provide scanning, filing and general warehouse administrative support.
- Communicate professionally with internal and external customers via telephone and email.
- Support excellent customer service standards and contribute towards a continuous improvement culture.

Skills & Experience

The ideal candidate will have:
- Previous experience in an administrative role, ideally within goods in, manufacturing, warehousing, logistics or a similar environment.
- Excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail.
- Confident verbal and written communication skills.
- A professional and friendly telephone manner.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and the ability to learn new systems.

What's on Offer?
- Highly competitive salary, dependent on experience.
- 25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays.
- Cycle to Work scheme.
- Life Assurance.
- Company discount scheme, offering savings on retail and leisure.
- Company pension scheme

title: Pharmacy Administrator
company: Navigo Health and Social Care CIC
advertiser_name: Navigo Health and Social Care CIC
description: 15 hours per week - Wednesday - Friday (hours to be agreed) An exciting opportunity has arisen for an organised and motivated Pharmacy Administrator to join our Pharmacy Team. In this role, you will play a key part in providing efficient administrative support and helping the team deliver high-quality services. We are looking for someone with excellent organisational skills, a keen eye for detail, and a positive, adaptable approach. If you enjoy working as part of a supportive team and are committed to delivering excellent administrative support, we would be delighted to hear from you. The Pharmacy Administrator will provide an efficient, accurate and confidential administrative service to the Lead Clinical Pharmacist and Pharmacy Team. The post holder will support the smooth running of pharmacy admin. Receive, record, process and distribute routine and non-routine information relating to pharmacy administration, including documents containing clinical and pharmaceutical terminology. Provide administrative support to the Lead Clinical Pharmacist and Pharmacy Team, including diary support, meeting co-ordination, minute taking at meetings, document preparation, audit support and maintenance of electronic records. Support the administration of pharmacy governance meetings, committees and medication-related policy processes under the direction of the Lead Clinical Pharmacist. Maintain accurate systems for pharmacy records, including prescription pad allocation, stock monitoring, distribution lists, action logs and relevant databases or spreadsheets. Act as a first point of administrative contact for internal and external pharmacy-related enquiries, resolving routine matters where appropriate and escalating queries outside agreed procedures. COMMUNICATION Monitor designated pharmacy email inboxes each working day, responding to routine enquiries within agreed administrative procedures and escalating clinical, medicines-related or governance queries to the Lead Clinical Pharmacist or Pharmacy Team. Communicate clearly and professionally with service users, carers, clinicians, managers, community services, external agencies and other stakeholders, ensuring messages are accurate, timely and appropriately recorded. Handle confidential and sensitive information in line with organisational policies, data protection requirements and information governance standards. Maintain regular communication with the Lead Clinical Pharmacist, including at least weekly contact to review current administrative priorities, outstanding actions, risks, issues and deadlines. Draft routine correspondence, responses and standard documents on behalf of the Pharmacy Team, seeking approval where required before circulation. PLANNING AND ORGANISATION Arrange pharmacy meetings, committees and forums, including room or online meeting set-up, calendar invites, agendas, papers, attendance records and distribution of documentation. Take accurate notes or minutes at pharmacy meetings, record decisions and actions, maintain action logs and follow up outstanding actions with the chair or action owner. Maintain circulation lists, distribution groups and contact lists for pharmacy meetings, forums and relevant communications. Prioritise own workload to meet agreed deadlines, seeking guidance where demands conflict or where issues require escalation. Support administrative preparation for audits, policy reviews, governance reports and other pharmacy-related workstreams as directed. GENERAL ADMINISTRATIVE DUTIES Maintain accurate electronic and paper records relating to pharmacy administration, ensuring information is filed, updated and retrievable in accordance with local procedures. Maintain databases and spreadsheets used by the Pharmacy Team, inputting and checking data accurately and escalating discrepancies or missing information. Produce, format and distribute correspondence, reports, presentations, meeting packs, action logs and other documents using Microsoft Office and relevant organisational systems. Support document control processes for medication-related policies, standard operating procedures and governance papers, including version control, circulation and approved storage locations. Ensure data entered or recorded by the post holder is relevant, accurate, complete and captured in a timely manner. Maintain accurate records of prescription pad allocation, receipt, issue and stock levels in accordance with organisational procedures. Arrange replenishment of prescription pad stock when required, escalating low stock, discrepancies, losses or governance concerns promptly to the Lead Clinical Pharmacist and Pharmacy Team. Support routine checks of pharmacy administrative stock and documentation, ensuring records are available for audit or governance review when requested. WORKFORCE Have input into training new team members on internal processes and procedures. PERSONAL RESPONSIBILITIES Complete and maintain mandatory training in line with organisational requirements, aiming to maintain personal compliance at or above the required organisational standard. Take responsibility for the quality, accuracy and timeliness of own work, seeking guidance where required. Work in accordance with Navigo values, code of conduct, policies, procedures and standards of professional behaviour. Maintain confidentiality at all times and comply with requirements relating to information governance, data protection, access to health records and records management. Comply with health and safety, fire safety, infection prevention and control, safeguarding, equality and diversity, business continuity, Mental Capacity Act and Deprivation of Liberty requirements relevant to the role. Participate in supervision, appraisal, personal development review and relevant training to support performance in the role.
